question: A house faces a 1-in-100 chance of flooding each year. Over a 30-year mortgage, what is the chance of at least one, in per cent?
answer: Chance of at least one: 1 − 0.74 = 0.26, about 26%.
move: Small yearly risks add up over every year of exposure.
ask: Which small yearly risk am I living with that adds up over the decades I'll face it?
trap: Reading a 100-year flood as one that comes once a century.
hint: Work out the chance of escaping every single year, then subtract it from one.
steps: Chance of no flood in one year: 0.99.
No flood in 30 years: 0.99 multiplied by itself 30 times ≈ 0.74.
Chance of at least one: 1 − 0.74 = 0.26, about 26%.
